title: fix(a2a): classify missing-url outbound rejections as permanent pre-dispatch
body:
## What Problem This Solves

#181175 — `sendA2aChannelText` rejects a peer without `url` (and a peer whose `outboundToken` reference did not resolve) with a plain `Error`. Both guards run before any I/O and depend only on loaded config, so no retry can ever succeed — yet the rejection matches neither the typed no-dispatch contract nor `isPermanentDeliveryError`'s text patterns. The outbound delivery queue therefore replays the send: the report shows one requester-settle wake retried twice (30 s, then 120 s) plus a dead-lettered session-event turn — four agent turns minted for one deterministic configuration failure.

## User Impact

A reply addressed to an inbound-only peer — the documented Quick-setup shape (`peers.<peer>.token` without `url`) — fails deterministically. Because the failure is classified retryable, each attempt costs a full agent turn and ends in a dead-letter entry instead of one terminal settlement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both pre-I/O config guards now throw `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` with `retryable: false` — the existing permanent no-dispatch contract (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/error-runtime`), the same pattern already used by the bundled feishu and googlechat channels for permanent pre-dispatch policy rejections:

- `findTerminalBatchRejection` settles the queued send terminally on the typed rejection (`src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts`), so no replay turns are minted.
- Queue-side behavior is already proven by `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` ("all-permanent batch" → terminal); this change makes the A2A producer speak that contract.
- The channel adapter (`extensions/a2a/src/channel.ts` send.text) and the cron announce route propagate the producer error unchanged, so no typed information is lost end to end.

The unresolved-`outboundToken` guard one statement below is the same deterministic pre-I/O config class and would spin the same retry loop, so it is classified in the same change.

## Evidence

- Red on base: the two strengthened tests in `extensions/a2a/src/outbound.test.ts` fail on the plain `Error` (verified by reverting only `outbound.ts` and running the suite: 2 failed / 8 passed).
- After fix: full A2A suite 86/86 across 2 shards; `outbound.test.ts` 10/10 on the exact pushed tree.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean; extensions oxlint clean; assertion-safety and test-mock-exports ratchets clean against the base.

### Real behavior proof (isolated Gateway, shipped entry points)

Isolated Gateway (loopback bind, throwaway state dir, synthetic config: peer `hermes` = token-only, no url; peer `prometheus` = url + unresolved `${A2A_PROOF_UNSET_TOKEN}` outboundToken) on the PR head. Both guards exercised through two shipped entry points:

**Gateway `send` RPC (`openclaw gateway call send`)** — both guards settle as permanent pre-dispatch failures with the typed code preserved through the delivery wrapper (gateway log):

```
⇄ res ✗ send 119ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE
  errorMessage=OutboundDeliveryError: peer hermes has no url configured for outbound A2A
  error=OutboundDeliveryError: … <- PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError:
       peer hermes has no url configured for outbound A2A:
       code=OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED

⇄ res ✗ send errorMessage=OutboundDeliveryError: peer prometheus outboundToken
  reference did not resolve; set the variable and reload before sending   → "retryable": false
```

**CLI (`openclaw message send --channel a2a`)** — both guards report the typed no-dispatch code with no network I/O:

```json
"error": "peer hermes has no url configured for outbound A2A | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED",
"sentBeforeError": false, "stage": "platform_send"
```

**No replay on later recovery passes**: 90 s after both sends (multiple queue recovery passes later) the durable queue holds zero entries for either peer, the log contains zero retry/replay/attempt lines for them, and no dead-letter was created — each send settled once, terminally, at first classification.

All names, tokens, and endpoints in the trace are synthetic (`prometheus.invalid`, throwaway state dir, loopback port); nothing to redact.

Closes #181175
